overall_summary: Space-themed content, specifically focusing on extreme exoplanet environments and immersive 'What If' scenarios, dominates the channel's performance. Shorter, generic psychology and trivia-style shorts struggle to gain traction, indicating that viewers crave high-stakes, visually spectacular cosmic mysteries over everyday facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,025 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views, 18 likes) are top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, first-person cosmic survival scenarios using extreme planetary conditions.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views, 25 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Frame planetary facts around sensational, tactile phenomena (e.g., raining rubies, glass, or iron) to spark immediate visual curiosity.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently flatline.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from soft psychology facts, or repackage them only if they can be framed as high-stakes survival/mystery scenarios.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (low engagement relative to space content).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard encyclopedia-style animal facts; transition instead to cinematic animal survival stories with high stakes.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Liquid Glass?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a cinematic, AI-generated POV of an astronaut falling through a beautiful but terrifying atmosphere where it rains sharp, molten glass sideways at 4,300 miles per hour.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the glass rain isn't even the deadliest part—the atmosphere is so hot it would vaporize your spacesuit before you even hit the ground.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'What If' format combined with extreme planetary weather (glass rain), matching the 21-second sweet spot that has proven to drive maximum views and likes.

experiment: Test a 'What If' format applied to a cinematic deep-sea mystery (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into the Mariana Trench?') to see if the high-stakes POV format translates successfully outside of space content.
